name: Optional advisory dod_ref key on five schemas

design_notes.plan_ref: definition-of-done-stateful-kettle.md F-094 ("optional dod_ref on five schemas") -- the sole scope-of-record for the five insertion sites, the identical key text, and the do-NOT-touch list. Feature 093 (standard/definition_of_done.md) landed at commit b451b96 and is status complete on .agent/feature_list_013.json; this contract's sole dependency is satisfied, and standard/definition_of_done.md now exists on disk at the path the dod_ref description text names.
design_notes.what_this_feature_is: The third feature of phase 013: adds an identically worded, optional, advisory `dod_ref` string property to five machine-validated schemas (contract, qa_verdict -- both anyOf branches, feature_list, work-packet, engineering_finding), touching zero `required` arrays, so the schema change is a pure loosening under methodology/06_release_train.md Section 3.2 (a new required key would be BREAKING per Section 3.1; a purely optional key is not). Proves the loosening with a positive fixture (tools/fixtures/feature_list_valid.json gains a dod_ref) that still validates and still passes the C16 --target sweep. Pairs one schema/README.md conventions-list sentence and a version bump/change_log entry (C8) documenting the new convention. Ships a CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] entry naming this feature (the file is concurrently edited by feature 097's implementation in a sibling work stream at proposal time; this contract names the file as scope but performs no conflicting edit now -- the append lands only when this contract's own implementation runs).
design_notes.dod_ref_wording: The exact, identical description string inserted at all six sites (verified against the plan and the task instruction, character-for-character): "Optional repo-relative path to the Definition of Done document governing this artifact's completion claims (in this repository `standard/definition_of_done.md`; in a bootstrapped consumer, conventionally `.nizam/standard/definition_of_done.md`). Advisory metadata: never required, and no check fails on its absence." The property itself: `"dod_ref": {"type": "string", "description": "<the string above>"}`. No `minLength`, `pattern`, or `format` constraint is added -- the key is advisory metadata only, per its own description, and a stricter constraint would risk narrowing what a consumer's path convention could name (the description names both the in-repo and the injected-consumer convention, but does not enumerate every possible layout a consumer might choose).

design_notes.additional_properties_confirmation: Independently re-verified today (not assumed) that every one of the six insertion sites sits inside an object schema declaring `"additionalProperties": true` at that exact nesting level: contract.schema.json line 131 (top level); qa_verdict.schema.json line 60 (legacy branch) and line 145 (evolved branch); feature_list.schema.json line 76 (top level); work-packet.schema.json line 107 (top level); engineering_finding.schema.json line 82 (top level). This is why the addition validates as a loosening without any schema needing its own edit beyond the new property declaration -- additionalProperties was already true everywhere dod_ref lands, so instances that already carried an undeclared dod_ref-shaped key (none are known to exist) were already tolerated; declaring it formally only adds documentation, a type constraint (`string`), and IDE/tooling discoverability.
design_notes.minor_safe_rationale: Per methodology/06_release_train.md Section 3.2 (verbatim standard cited by both the plan Context and the phase-013 product spec's Public contract changes section): a schema change that adds an optional key and touches no `required` array is a loosening and is MINOR-safe -- every artifact that validated before this change continues to validate after it, because the new key's absence is always permitted. Section 3.1 of the same document classifies a new REQUIRED key as BREAKING; this contract adds zero required-array entries anywhere, mechanically proven by acceptance test 3 below (a script-level scan of every `required` array in every schema/*.schema.json file for the literal token `dod_ref`), not merely asserted in prose.
design_notes.do_not_touch_list: The phase, debt, and capability_profile schemas (schema/phase.schema.json, schema/debt.schema.json, schema/capability_profile.schema.json) are deliberately excluded from this feature's five-schema scope. Per the phase-013 plan's Out of scope section and product_spec_013.md's own 'Out of scope' section, these three declare `additionalProperties: false` by DD-3 design (phase.schema.json's own DD-3 Evidence Externalisation docstring in schema/README.md explains why: a closed property set is load-bearing there, closing the gap that let inline terminal-output payloads hide inside an unrecognised key). Adding dod_ref to a closed-schema document would require also adding it to that document's own `properties` AND would still validate identically whether or not the schema formally admits it, since a closed schema rejects ANY unlisted key -- so touching these three would be schema-shape work outside this feature's stated scope (five named schemas, not eight), and this contract's verification (acceptance test 2 below) mechanically asserts these three files are byte-identical to base_revision, so no accidental edit lands.
design_notes.dogfood_note: Per the phase-013 execution choreography (plan Section 'Execution choreography', step 3): 'dod_ref set from F-094 onward -- dogfooding'. This contract's own implementation does not itself set dod_ref on any .agent/contracts/NNN.json or .agent/qa/NNN.json it produces (that is a QA-time and Generator-Step-7 convention for feature 094 onward, not a requirement this contract's OWN scope mandates on itself at proposal time -- the schema must exist before any artifact can legally carry the key). Recorded here so a future reviewer does not read this contract's own JSON as non-compliant for omitting dod_ref: the key becomes available only once this contract's implementation lands, and its first legitimate use is this very contract's post-implementation QA verdict (.agent/qa/094.json), authored after the schema change is live.
design_notes.ndebt_040_compliance: This contract's own verification includes NO byte-guard anchored on .agent/run_state.json. NDEBT-040 (docs/planning/DEBT.md, OPEN, adjudicated for contract 093) prescribes: 'byte-guards in contracts scope to feature lists only (the 092 precedent)', because the Orchestrator legitimately appends coordination records to run_state.json continuously between contract approval and QA, making a run_state byte-guard unsatisfiable for reasons unattributable to the implementation. This contract's non_goals carve-out (below) mirrors contract 092's original correctly-scoped pattern: a feature-list byte-guard only (`.agent/feature_list*.json` byte-identical to base_revision), with run_state and phase_013.yaml explicitly named as non-goals rather than guarded, matching the 092 precedent NDEBT-040 itself cites as correct.
design_notes.backward_compat_mechanism: The full default `bash tools/validate.sh` sweep already re-validates every historical `.agent/contracts/*.json` and `.agent/qa/*.json` file against the (now-edited) contract.schema.json and qa_verdict.schema.json via check C11 (`check_c11_dogfood_sweep`, tools/validate.sh, glob-based over `.agent/contracts/*.json` and, when the directory exists, `.agent/qa/*.json`), and every `.agent/feature_list*.json` file against the (now-edited) feature_list.schema.json via check C16 (`vlib_feature_list_lifecycle`, tools/verify_lib.sh, invoked by check_c16_feature_list_lifecycle). Because both checks are glob-based over the real `.agent/` tree, not enumerated by a fixed list, a purely additive/optional schema change that broke any historical artifact would surface as a C11 or C16 FAIL in the same `bash tools/validate.sh` run this contract's own acceptance tests already require to report `SUMMARY: 16 passed, 0 failed`. Independently re-counted on disk at base_revision today (not trusted from the plan's Context, which predates the 094/095/096/097 contract-negotiation activity now in flight): 64 files under `.agent/contracts/*.json`, 117 files under `.agent/qa/*.json`, 13 files matching `.agent/feature_list*.json`. Because siblings 095/096/097 may add further contracts/QA files concurrently before this feature's own implementation lands, the verification below asserts `>=` these counts, not `==`, so it remains satisfiable regardless of sibling landing order while still proving the sweep is non-vacuous.
